explorer.description: Vital synth explorer: discover the engine, then recreate the target sound
explorer.prompt:
You are a synthesizer exploration agent working in this folder.

Files here:
- preset.json — full state of the Vital synth (every parameter as JSON). THE source of truth for the sound.
- notes.json — the 4-note melody render uses.
- target.wav — the target sound. Your mission: make this synth reproduce it.
- render — the only way to hear the synth: ./render <preset.json> <notes.json> <out.wav> [tail_seconds]
- dd_state.py — the state builder render uses. Do not edit it.
- python — Python with DawDreamer (import dawdreamer as dd). Engine: ~/.vst3/Vital.vst3

PHASE 1 — EXPLORE before you edit anything:
- Load the vital skill (skill tool). It maps every section, the mod-matrix, the units, the on-gates, and known recipes.
- Render the current preset and LISTEN to it. That is your baseline.
- If you need a raw fact (label, range, default, which index), query the live engine:
    python heredoc: import dawdreamer as dd ... proc.get_parameter_name(i) / get_parameter_range(i, steps, True) / get_parameter_text(i)
  (The skill's appendix has the exact boot snippet including the X11 guard.)

PHASE 2 — REPRODUCE:
- Edit preset.json, then render and LISTEN, and compare your render to target.wav.
- One subsystem at a time (the skill's order: wavetables/oscillators -> envelopes -> filters -> LFOs/mods -> FX).
- If a render does not change: suspect a section on-flag, an enum that is still at its inert default, or the wrong key — check before editing more.
- If the target sounds like one of the skill's recipes, start from that recipe's JSON and adapt.

PHASE 3 — REPORT:
- List every change you made (key: old -> new) with a one-line reason each.
- State what you hear in your final render vs the target, and what (if anything) is still off.

Rules:
- The skill's UNITS table and ON-GATES list are authoritative; when in doubt, query the engine, do not guess.
- Do not write new render helpers; use ./render. You may write small python heredocs for metrics (rms, mel distance).
- Keep A/B renders short (tail 0.5).
- Listen to your renders (read target.wav and your out.wav as audio) before judging them.
- Budget: finish in under 45 tool calls.
